title: Linear congruences and solution counts
section: Part A: Number Theory ▷ The Congruence Equation ax = b (mod n)
terms: linear congruence; modular inverse; number of congruence solutions.

exposition.text:
Let d = gcd(a, n) with n > 0. The congruence ax ≡ b (mod n) has a solution exactly when d | b.
When solvable, divide all three quantities by d and invert a/d modulo n/d; this gives one class
modulo n/d.
In the original modulus n, that class consists of exactly d distinct solutions, separated by n/d.
Thus uniqueness modulo n/d must not be confused with uniqueness modulo n. Bounds such as
L < x < U reduce the final step to counting members of an arithmetic progression.

question.text:
How many residues x modulo 126 satisfy 42x ≡ 84 (mod 126)?
(A) 1 (B) 3 (C) 21 (D) 42 (E) 63

solution.text:
Here d = 42, and 42 | 84. Dividing gives x ≡ 2 (mod 3), which has 126/3 = 42 representa-
tives modulo 126.

question.text:
Which of the following integers x with 100 < x < 150 satisfies 35x ≡ 10 (mod 55)?
(A) 103 (B) 112 (C) 115 (D) 127 (E) 143

For how many residue classes b modulo 60 does 24x ≡ b (mod 60) have exactly twelve solution
classes modulo 60?
(A) 1 (B) 5 (C) 12 (D) 24 (E) 60

solution.text:
The coefficient gcd is twelve. The congruence is solvable exactly for the five multiples
of twelve modulo sixty: 0, 12, 24, 36, 48. Each such right-hand side has twelve preimages.
The question counts permissible right-hand sides, rather than the solutions for one fixed
right-hand side.

question.text:
For an integer n > 1, how many ordered pairs of residues (a, b) modulo n make x 7→ ax + b a
permutation of all residue classes modulo n?
2
(A) φ(n) (B) n (C) nφ(n) (D) n (E) n − φ(n)

solution.text:
Translation by b is always a permutation, with inverse translation by −b. Multiplication by
a is a permutation exactly when gcd(a, n) = 1: then every linear congruence has a unique
solution; otherwise the congruence ax = 0 has more than one solution. There are φ(n)
choices for a and independently n for b, giving nφ(n).

question.text:
How many solution classes of 12x ≡ 12 (mod 60) are represented by integers relatively prime to
60?
(A) 3 (B) 4 (C) 5 (D) 8 (E) 12

solution.text:
Divide the congruence by twelve to obtain x ≡ 1 (mod 5). Such residues already avoid
the prime five. CRT pairs this fixed residue modulo five with any residue modulo twelve;
exactly φ(12) = 4 of those are coprime to twelve. Thus four of the twelve original solutions
are units modulo sixty: 1, 11, 31, 41.
